short.q: Explain why the bleep test is not always a good measure of fitness for a footballer.
short.model: It tests only cardiovascular fitness in a straight-line shuttle run, so it is not sport-specific and does not measure skills like power or agility.

short.q: Describe how to carry out the Cooper 12-minute run.
short.model: Run as far as possible around a marked track in 12 minutes, then record the distance covered in metres.

short.q: A student's sit and reach score rises from 6 cm to 12 cm. State what this shows and calculate the percentage change.
short.model: Flexibility has improved. The change is (12 − 6) ÷ 6 × 100 = 100%.

short.q: Explain why power is important to a volleyball player.
short.model: Power lets her jump high quickly to spike or block, combining strength and speed in the take-off.

short.q: Give two ways to make a fitness test more reliable.
short.model: Use the same equipment, surface, tester, warm-up and time of day each time, and give the same instructions.
points: any specific factor e.g. same tester/equipment
